title: Carrot Cake
subtitle: Spiced carrot cake with cream cheese frosting
excerpt: A dense, moist spiced cake packed with grated carrot, walnuts, and cinnamon, topped with a tangy cream cheese and icing sugar frosting. One of Britain's favourite cakes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Carrot cake has medieval European origins: sugar was expensive, so sweetness came from vegetables. The modern British version, with cream cheese frosting, developed through American influence in the 20th century and became a coffeehouse staple in the 1990s. The carrots serve two purposes: they add sweetness and their moisture makes the crumb dense and tender. Do not squeeze the grated carrot dry: the moisture is part of the recipe.

content.text: Use oil rather than butter: oil keeps the cake moist for longer and gives a denser crumb that is characteristic of carrot cake. Grate the carrots finely rather than coarsely for a more even texture. The cream cheese frosting should be thick enough to spread without running: if it is too soft, chill the frosting for 20 minutes before using.
Heat the oven to 175 C / fan 155 C / gas 4. Grease and line two 20 cm sandwich tins.
Whisk together the eggs, oil, and both sugars until well combined. Fold in the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and salt. Stir in the grated carrot and walnuts.
Divide between the tins. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely before frosting.
Beat the cream cheese, butter, and icing sugar together until smooth. Spread over one cooled layer. Place the second layer on top. Spread the remaining frosting over the top and sides.
